record.original_question: Can large finite monodromy extensions arising from these curve-cover constructions be used in the classical inverse Galois problem to produce field extensions with a prescribed type of ramification at a specified place?

evidence.quote: An affirmative answer to question 6.17 would allow us to produce finite monodromy extensions L/K with big Galois groups, hence Galois extensions of K^tame with big Galois groups.

artifact.category_tag: Inverse Galois problem with prescribed ramification
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $K^{\mathrm{tame}}$ denote a maximal tamely ramified extension of $K$ inside a fixed algebraic closure. Suppose one has a construction that, starting from suitable finite (possibly wildly ramified) Galois covers of smooth projective curves over the residue field, produces finite Galois extensions $L/K$ whose Galois groups $G = \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ realize prescribed finite groups as monodromy groups, together with control over the ramification filtration (in particular the higher ramification groups in upper numbering) at the closed point.

The problem is the following: Given a number field $k$ and a place $v$ of $k$, together with a finite group $G$ and a prescribed conjugacy-invariant datum $\mathcal{R}$ describing the desired local ramification behaviour at $v$ (e.g. inertia subgroup, wild inertia, jumps in the upper-numbering filtration), determine whether the curve-cover monodromy construction described above can be used to produce a finite Galois extension $M/k$ with $\mathrm{Gal}(M/k) \cong G$ whose decomposition/inertia data at $v$ realize $\mathcal{R}$. Equivalently: can such wild-monodromy constructions be applied to the classical inverse Galois problem to yield Galois extensions of a global field with a specified type of ramification at a specified place?
artifact.status_search_result: The inverse Galois problem with prescribed local ramification (especially wild ramification) at specified places remains an active and largely open area. While there is substantial progress on realizing groups via covers with prescribed ramification (e.g., Hurwitz space methods, Belyi map computations, and recent classifications of monodromy groups of indecomposable covers), no general answer is known for arbitrary groups and arbitrary prescribed wild ramification types. The question as posed is broad and appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Park City lecture notes: Around the inverse Galois problem
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the inverse Galois problem indicating that producing extensions with prescribed local behaviour is a major theme with many open cases.
status_evidence.claim: Realising groups with prescribed local ramification is an active topic with many open instances.

status_evidence.title: Computation of Belyi maps with prescribed ramification and applications in Galois theory
status_evidence.snippet: Computes families of covers with prescribed ramification and applies them to inverse Galois questions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists via explicit covers with prescribed ramification, but the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Monodromy groups of indecomposable coverings of bounded genus
status_evidence.snippet: Classifies monodromy groups and ramification types of indecomposable covers in high degree.
status_evidence.claim: Recent classification results constrain which monodromy/ramification data are realizable.
